# Closing-record evidence audit — final_coverage

**Approve records and core fit for both exact closing pins below.** I found no evidence inflation, lost regression evidence, or new implementation hidden in these record changes. This approval does not certify subsequent commits, hosted checks, publication, or the owner's checkout.

| Layer | Closing revision | Reviewed implementation revision | Records verdict | Independent core-fit verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower | `a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5` | `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42` | approve | approve |
| Upper | `87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd` | `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41` | approve | approve |

Reviewer identity: **final_coverage**. Scope: independent evidence-fidelity/completeness and core-fit review of the closing records. Inputs were the mechanical closing packets and revision manifest, immutable clone files/contracts/Git objects, and my own original reports and raw evidence. Captured reports from other reviewers were treated as historical data; I did not use their verdicts as authority or consult their new closing verdicts or worker narratives.

The records now preserve the executed code reviews and distinguish them from later record publication. Both code snapshots are unchanged, so my prior bounded code conclusions carry forward only through the explicit source audit below. The additional external review remains explicitly unexecuted; its question withholds only transmission to the external service.

## Source and original-check preservation

- Lower changed 28 paths and upper changed 45 paths relative to their respective code pins. Every changed path is under `tasks`, `memory`, `message-queue`, `roadmap`, or `history`; none is executable or protocol code outside those record roots.
- All 96 tracked entries selected by the automation/template/skill/handbook/service/workflow/adapter roots and all `AGENTS.md` contracts match in mode, type and Git object identity in each layer. No code, test, ownership mapping, template, hook or admission protocol changed.
- All 538 lower and 586 upper `ReconcileQueueTests` method sources are unchanged from their respective code pins. All 507 original PR88 method names remain in lower; all 512 original PR89 method names remain in upper. The recovery additions remain exactly 31 lower methods and 74 upper methods, measured against those different original bases, not additive stack totals.
- Relative to each code pin, all existing history entries (120 lower; 121 upper), 41 decision entries, 20 human-queue entries, and 283 completed-task entries retain their exact mode/type/blob. The only new human item is the external-review authorization question. The upper adds one new handover; no old handover changes.
- The six checked moved-worklog copies preserve their entire original byte prefix (two lower and four upper). Both original PR task verification records retain their complete prior byte prefix in the upper closing tree. Closing records therefore do not erase old results or turn them into newly executed checks.

## Imported regression evidence

**Lower:** all three declared raw-evidence SHA-256 values match my original scratch artifacts. All 29 initial green rows and all 29 associated failing-control rows match the original observations exactly, including each fault identity. Their green checkpoint remains explicitly `e126316ce6fa724b19353501a817ab89a6f08af3`, not relabeled as the later code or closing revision. The historical rollback produced 19 failing methods; targeted faults produced the remaining 10. These were localized reconciler rollbacks retaining the candidate shared modules/templates, not pristine historical-tree runs.

The initial focused green result is 29/29 methods, 389 subcases, zero assertion failures, errors or skips. The two separately recorded Unicode methods match my original lower-r2 logs: 2/2 green and 28 subcases on each of Python 3.14.6 and 3.9.6; restoring the older interpreter-dependent format-control predicate gives 2/2 failing methods and 24/28 failing subcases on Python 3.9.6, with zero errors/skips. Their method names complete the independently recomputed 31-method addition set. The lower map honestly distinguishes these later methods and the later full-runner revision from the initial 29-method run.

**Upper:** the imported map is a byte-for-byte copy of my original final-r4 map, not merely a matching summary:

```text
bytes: 59166
SHA-256: 4d011ff0f51657ee2c66549b366c8e3162fdcc08e7cb110e185d5ff7116db75f
candidate: 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41
lower: 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42
```

I rechecked all 74 method source hashes against the closing clone, both candidate result arrays per method, every primary failing-control array and fault source pin, and all seven run summaries against my raw result JSON. All match. Both interpreters retain 74/74 green methods and 1,072 subcases, with zero errors/skips. Every one of the 74 distinct methods has an observed assertion failure under its recorded relevant control; no failure is inferred from an error, skip or empty selection. Historical and mutant runs overlap, so their run counts are not summed into a fictitious distinct-method total.

Runner discovery remains the previously observed 74/74 recovery methods out of 586 total methods. The five recorded input-to-test ownership mappings, seven exact commands/environments, deliberate control semantics, Unicode exhaustive comparisons, and three-per-interpreter guidance probes are all retained byte-for-byte in the map. This closing audit validates the existing evidence and unchanged sources; it does not claim fresh execution of those runtime probes.

## Captured reports and scope honesty

All 15 JSON capture files across the two clones (10 distinct report contents, including five inherited lower captures in upper) have valid declared UTF-8 content hashes and the correct layer-specific code-pin metadata. All three copies of my two distinct reports match my originals byte-for-byte:

```text
lower report SHA-256:
7519eb544acad88e0d11e2ea766cb02bf81fd01fede1a9a2b5b5e98f4493f28b
upper report SHA-256:
a877b6cc361718460470afee8b212b2719ae91b9390397cb6d46030f72c0834a
```

The lower capture correctly preserves my older upper failure rather than rewriting history; the lower verification text explicitly limits that capture to its lower conclusion. Upper instead captures my final `4008f498` report. For the other eight distinct reviewer reports, I verified capture self-hashes and revision metadata, not independent authorship or the truth of their runtime claims; those verdicts are not evidence for this approval.

The verification records identify code pins and reserve later record checks/publication for later evidence. The hosted snapshot names `5a9f044f` and `4008f498`, and is expressly not evidence for the closing revisions. It distinguishes native approval counts from GitHub reviews. The normal-suite five intentional skips are disclosed; separate corpus/projection executions are identified, and the macOS filename limit remains explicit. The lower record does not claim it independently ran the upper's opt-in projection check. No record-only or empty-selection result is presented as runtime coverage.

The source-fidelity limits are preserved: no external fetching or truth/relevance judgment; lexical literal recognition and exact-spacing fallback for ambiguous R-prefix prose; explicit Unicode 16 scope. The authorization record keeps the answer blank, names `operation:external-recovery-code-review`, and points to an existing stable evidence file. It grants no implicit transmission or merge authority and claims no Claude verdict. Both closing-range repository checks accepted the new records; the upper check also accepted the new handover's queue projection.

## Commands actually executed for this audit

All repository checks below used this prefix, with no installer, checkout/index/config mutation, bytecode writes, network calls or test-suite reruns:

```sh
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14
```

Environment: Darwin arm64, Git 2.55.0, Python 3.14.6. My retained runtime evidence also identifies system `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6. The following arguments were appended to the prefix:

```text
cwd: /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-closing
automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition merge --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack --range 5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5
exit 0; 0 blocking findings, 5 advisories

cwd: /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing
automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check --at-transition merge --branch task/2026-08-30-repair-human-question-evidence --range 4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41...87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd
exit 0; 0 blocking findings, 6 advisories

cwd: /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-lower-closing
automation/check_core_scope.py --range 326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12...a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5 --branch task/2026-08-30-rebuild-the-open-pr-stack
exit 0; pass, 11 core paths; independent review manual, not invoked

cwd: /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-closing
automation/check_core_scope.py --range a202233c10705e544b2292734cacbe698218b9a5...87c398c091872314defb3e94062ed7310c0f83fd --branch task/2026-08-30-repair-human-question-evidence
exit 0; pass, 10 core paths; independent review manual, not invoked

cwd: /private/tmp
/private/tmp/final-coverage-closing-audit.py > /private/tmp/final-coverage-closing-audit.log
final exit 0; 0 failed assertions; JSON result: /private/tmp/final-coverage-closing-audit.json
```

The scratch audit uses read-only `git --no-replace-objects -C <clone> rev-parse`, `diff --name-only`, `ls-tree -r -z`, `show`, and `diff --quiet --exit-code HEAD`, plus AST/source and SHA-256 comparisons. Both final tracked-clean checks returned 0. An initial scratch comparison incorrectly assumed normalized key names for ten lower mutant-control rows; the imported records preserve their original `skips`/`red_subcases` keys. Correcting that comparator to compare the original schema produced the final zero-failure result; no reviewed record was changed.

Fresh closing audit count: 2/2 repository-range checks and 2/2 core-schema checks passed; 29/29 lower initial result pairs, 74/74 upper method/result/control rows, 7/7 upper run summaries, 15/15 capture hashes and 3/3 own-report copies validated. No unit test was selected or run in this closing audit, and none is represented as a new pass or skip.

## Independent core fit and remaining limits

For **lower**, the updated task/design still describe portable Markdown/Git/Python queue protections and authoring rules. Capturing code-review evidence and an unanswered external-disclosure question introduces no provider-specific execution mechanism or user-global state. The historical record may name Claude or GitHub without making either a core dependency. Agent, provider and unrelated-repository substitution remain credible: approve.

For **upper**, the updated design accurately bounds candidate-file citations, lexical quote fidelity and unanswered review identity. The record changes neither widen semantic claims nor move advisory source checks into blocking enforcement. Its mechanisms and durable evidence remain usable by other agents, providers and adopted repositories, without a new adapter or user-global write: approve.

These are my independent judgments after reading the changed task/design inputs, not conclusions borrowed from captured reports or from the schema checker. The parent still owns the revision-bound receipt, final actual publication/CI/admission ranges, original-owner index/probes/refs preservation, and any external-review authorization. I did not rerun full suites or the full runtime panel, verify current hosted status, prove the execution refusal from an external provider log, or certify original copies of other reviewers' reports. Those limits do not create a code or record defect in the two pinned closing deltas examined here.
